key_insight: The paper introduces Forward CIP (F-CIP), an RL-native intrinsic motivation objective that uses system dynamics alone to enable unsupervised discovery of controllable, primitive behaviors without hand-designed reward signals.
engineering_relevance: F-CIP reduces reward-engineering burden for robotics and control by helping agents learn useful behaviors like balancing, hopping, and running from intrinsic objectives plus minimal task rewards.
method: Reformulate Controllable Information Production as a forward RL objective (F-CIP).
Use intrinsic motivation derived from environment dynamics rather than selecting domain-specific information variables.
Combine F-CIP with existing RL algorithms and, for locomotion, a simple forward-velocity reward.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that agents trained with F-CIP autonomously discover primitive behaviors and, when paired with a simple forward-velocity reward, learn coordinated gaits such as hopping and running that would otherwise need reward engineering.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on the underlying dynamics and RL setup, so stability and scalability across diverse environments should be validated.
paper_title: Bellman Meets Lyapunov: Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning via Mastering Chaos
